# team-rollout: what it prints

<!-- Generated by scripts/render_demos.py from real runs; do not edit by
     hand. CI fails when this file no longer matches the code. -->

Real output of [team-rollout](../../plugins/team-rollout) on the fixtures its own
tests use. Skills and subagents are not shown: what they say depends on the
model, and they are measured by the eval cases in the plugin's `evals/`.

## check_settings.py on a settings file that is wider than intended

Errors are what should never ship; warnings are grants to narrow.

```console
$ python3 plugins/team-rollout/scripts/check_settings.py plugins/team-rollout/tests/fixtures/bad-settings.json
ERROR  dangerouslySkipPermissions  [dangerous-flag]
        dangerouslySkipPermissions is true, which bypasses every permission check
        → Remove it. If a specific workflow needs it, scope it to that workflow rather than the whole configuration.
ERROR  env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY  [secret-value]
        a literal credential appears in this file
        → Settings files get committed and shared. Reference an environment variable instead, and rotate this value — it should be treated as leaked.
ERROR  hooks.Stop[0]  [relative-hook]
        hook command is a relative path: './scripts/gate.sh'
        → It resolves against whatever directory the session started in. Use "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/… — quoted, because the path can contain a space.
ERROR  permissions.defaultMode  [bypass-default]
        defaultMode is 'bypassPermissions'
        → This disables the permission system for every session using this file. Acceptable inside a disposable VM, never as a default.
warn   env.PROXY_TOKEN  [secret-key]
        env.PROXY_TOKEN holds a literal value
        → A key with this name should reference the environment, not carry the value.
warn   permissions.allow[Bash]  [broad-allow]
        'Bash' allows the whole tool, not a pattern
        → Grant the narrowest form that works — Bash(npm test:*) rather than Bash. A blanket allow never gets narrowed back once someone has stopped being prompted.
warn   permissions.allow[Read(*)]  [broad-allow]
        'Read(*)' allows the whole tool, not a pattern
        → Grant the narrowest form that works — Bash(npm test:*) rather than Bash. A blanket allow never gets narrowed back once someone has stopped being prompted.
warn   permissions.allow[Write]  [broad-allow]
        'Write' allows the whole tool, not a pattern
        → Grant the narrowest form that works — Bash(npm test:*) rather than Bash. A blanket allow never gets narrowed back once someone has stopped being prompted.
note   hooks.Stop[0]  [no-timeout]
        no timeout on a hook that can block a session
        → Give it one. A hook that hangs on this event leaves the session unable to finish.

1 file(s): 4 error(s), 5 to look at
[exit 1]
```
